--- title: "Arabic numeral naming" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · MATE_ET_VERB_ARABIGOS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_ET_VERB_ARABIGOS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Lectura de números arábigos*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_ET_VERB_ARABIGOS.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Arabic numeral naming, from age 4 to 5 (3,029 administrations in 5 cohorts). AUC .65–.74 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1676 | | Battery | ORZA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 11 (1676) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child names numbers 0—10 as shown on the screen. Number of right answers is registered. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:----------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1676|Arábigos |Un dibujo por pantalla | 11| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 5| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1676.** Números del 0 al 10 en orden fijo; el evaluador marca sí/no (proyecto ORZA). *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1676 · Arábigos](../../figuras/plataforma/1676.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1676"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Counting forwards and backwards, and reading Arabic numerals, measure **symbolic number knowledge**: the verbal sequence of numerals and its correspondence with digits. This is learned knowledge, distinct from the approximate number sense (comparing quantities), and it forms the basis of school arithmetic. **What the evidence says:** - **Counting in preschool predicts mathematics in the first school years.** Mastery of counting principles at age 5 predicts the risk of mathematical difficulties in Grade 1 [@stock2009markers]. In Spanish children, the verbal number sequence (procedural counting) was the preschool task with the most weight in Grade 2 mathematics achievement [@mercader2017basicas]. - **Knowing Arabic numerals is one of the two pillars of early arithmetic.** In 569 children, only number knowledge and quantity discrimination uniquely predicted arithmetic progress in the first school year [@malone2020number]. Children with mathematical difficulties already show symbolic deficits in preschool, and those deficits persist [@desoete2012comparison]. - **Counting backwards is more demanding** than counting forwards. It requires retrieving the sequence in reverse order and holding it in working memory, which is why it discriminates better at age 5. **What our data show.** The four tasks have high internal consistency (α = .84–.95), but they were given in one or two sessions and there is no stability between terms. They predict later reading fluency poorly (AUC .53–.59), which supports their discriminant validity. Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11, counting backwards in the second ten is the most specific: AUC .67 vs. .51 for reading ([Numerical cognition](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.3| 2011| 141|2015/16 | 808| 0| 808| 33| | 4.3| 2012| 158|2016/17 | 384| 380| 0| 17| | 4.3| 2013| 191|2017/18 | 582| 571| 11| 23| | 4.3| 2014| 627|2018/19 | 389| 0| 389| 20| | 5.3| 2010| 140|2015/16 | 866| 258| 606| 36| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.3| 951| 2012, 2013| 8.87| 2.55| 10| -1.33| 1.16| 39.75| | 5.3| 258| 2010| 10.60| 1.10| 11| -4.00| 0.00| 80.62| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–11 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range |Warning | |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|:--------------------| | 4.3| 951|0–11 |0–11 |0–11 | | | 5.3| 258|6–11 |2–11 |0–11 |extreme value: check | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .84. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Letter knowledge (4.3, r = .52); Letter knowledge (5.3, r = .38). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .65–.74. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .57–.62. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ET_VERB_ARABIGOS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .53–.65 (2 time points; 219–414 children). Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([provisional criterion](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*), AUC .58–.64. ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.3| 951| 2012, 2013| 4| 5| 6| 8| 10| 11| 11| | 5.3| 258| 2010| 9| 10| 10| 11| 11| 11| 11| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ET_VERB_ARABIGOS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 2,018| 0.070| 0.002| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 2,088| 0.019| 0.656| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 2,107| 0.193| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 2,163| 0.099| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 866| 0.138| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 827| 0.003| 0.969| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 826| 0.108| 0.002| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 866| 0.075| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Arabic numeral naming” (code 1676; ORZA battery) assesses number transcoding. Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 11 items. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 5 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .84 (N = 1,365, 11 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.62. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 5.3: the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - Ceiling effect at 4.3, 5.3 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
